subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw standardize a machine-readable Skill Workshop proposal lifecycle contract in core, and should that contract be AISP/AISOP or an OpenClaw-native docs/test artifact?
rationale: The current code already enforces many lifecycle rules, but making them an authoritative machine-readable contract affects security review, package ownership, ClawHub/core boundaries, and future compatibility semantics.

options.title: OpenClaw-native contract first
options.body: Add a narrow repo-owned lifecycle contract fixture plus docs/tests for the existing service invariants, without adding AISP as runtime or required package surface.

options.title: Keep it outside core
options.body: Treat the AISP/AISOP example as an optional ClawHub or external reference package and leave OpenClaw core with prose docs plus targeted tests.

options.title: Adopt AISP/AISOP in core
options.body: Add a standard AISP/AISOP package under the Skill Workshop area, accepting a new external protocol-shaped security/product contract.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native contract first
recommendation.body: Add a narrow repo-owned lifecycle contract fixture plus docs/tests for the existing service invariants, without adding AISP as runtime or required package surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and carried the central Skill Workshop lifecycle implementation and are the strongest history-backed owner for deciding the contract boundary.
